analysis:
The PR only modifies docs/architecture/inference.md (patch hunks at @@ -22 and @@ -718). It adds a description of the unregistered Nemotron Super local bridge, load owner, image binding, MTP and concurrency environment variables. It also changes the TemplateRenderCheck sentence to say multimodal fixtures run when the shared media discovery policy accepts the configuration, instead of only when config.json declares vision_config. No code or control change is visible in the supplied units.

Relevant threats and assets: TB-007 (inference engine), TB-003 (in-process media decode and operator), T-050, T-041 and A-001. The doc states these properties:
- No model registration and no HTTP route. NemotronSuperLocalImageHTTP defaults to absent and has no production caller.
- Authenticated local application. Ingress, media and speculation charges happen before decode. Only data:image/png and data:image/jpeg base64 URIs are accepted. Container limits are checked before raster allocation.
- Prefix reuse is rejected for these paths, so the T-041 cache surface is unchanged.
- Speculation (MTP) is opt-in via DARKBLOOM_NEMOTRON_SUPER_MTP=1, and media is refused with mediaWithSpeculation.

Coverage limit: the referenced Swift sources (NemotronSuperLocalBridgeBuilder, NemotronSuperImageDecode, NemotronSuperLocalImageHTTP and others) were not supplied. The doc's claims about authentication, default-off, unregistered status and bounds are unverified here. The code PR that introduces them should be checked for:
- in-process PNG/ImageIO decode of untrusted bytes on TB-003/TB-007;
- whether the local HTTP hook can ever be exposed in production;
- whether the env-var concurrency up to 64 interacts with the KV and memory admission budgets;
- whether the template-check change to media discovery policy alters what the capacity quote advertises.

No security regression or threat-model invalidation is evident from the documentation alone.
